hero.caption: An American flag flies over Gate 17 of Terminal A at Newark Liberty International Airport. On September 11, 2001, United Airlines Flight 93 pushed back from the gate at 8:01 am, headed for San Francisco. Passengers learned about the coordinated attacks, and tried to overtake the airplane, resulting in the plane crashing into a field in Shanksville, Pennsylvania.

images.caption: As a member of the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Honor Guard, National Wildlife Refuge System Law Enforcement Officer Shelby Finney helped dedicate a Pennsylvania memorial to passengers of Flight 93, killed by terrorists on September 11. Finney, based at Salt Plains National Wildlife Refuge in Oklahoma, was named 2011 Officer of the Year for the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service’s Southwest Region. (USFWS)

images.filename: With This Plaque, Memories of the Heroes of Flight 93 Will Remain Etched in the Walls of the U.S. Capitol (3909403659).jpg
images.caption:
On Wednesday, Speaker Pelosi joined with Senator Kent Conrad (D-ND), Congressman Bill Shuster (R-PA), Gordon Felt, President of Families of Flight 93 and family members of the heroes of Flight 93 for a plaque dedication ceremony for victims of United Airlines Flight 93, which crashed on September 11, 2001.   
Senator Kent Conrad of North Dakota and Congressman Bill Shuster of Pennsylvania authored bipartisan legislation that called for a location in the Capitol to be named in the memory of the crew and passengers of Flight 93, and a commemorative plaque to be placed at that location. 
Speaker Pelosi at the dedication:
“Today we gather to unveil a marker of bravery; to remember acts of unmatched courage; and to recall the men and women of United Airlines Flight 93 – some of the true heroes of September 11, 2001.
“With this plaque, the memories of the heroes of Flight 93 will forever remain etched in the walls of the U.S. Capitol – as a beacon of hope in the heart and soul of our democracy.
“Their names will be forever etched in the hearts of their families and loved ones – and now on a plaque in our nation’s temple of freedom, where all who visit can honor their sacrifice.
“Their heroic deeds are their true memorial.  Their bravery, their sacrifice, their willingness to put their lives on the line to protect victims unknown and families unseen – these will be their eternal monument and their enduring contribution.
“For those of us who work here in the Capitol – the target of Flight 93 – we will remain eternally grateful for the heroes of that flight, for their courage and character.

“May God bless their memory. May God bless us all with their strength.  May God continue to bless the United States of America.”

images.caption: View looking southeast along the flight path of Flight 93.  The black wall borders the debris field.  The boulder at the right marks the impact site and the grave of the 33 passengers and crew, and the gate is opened once annually on September 11 for family members to lay wreaths.  Beyond the boulder is the hemlock grove.   Flight 93 National Memorial, 6424 Lincoln Hwy, Stoystown, Pa. 17 September 2020
